questions.stem: Which statement is logically equivalent to P implies Q? (case 34)
questions.explanation: The contrapositive of P implies Q is: if not Q then not P, and it is logically equivalent. The converse and inverse are not equivalent in general.
questions.hint: Negate and swap the antecedent and consequent.

questions.stem: Given P implies Q and P, which conclusion is valid? (case 50)
questions.explanation: Modus ponens lets us conclude Q from P implies Q together with P. Denying the antecedent and affirming the consequent are invalid argument forms.
questions.hint: An implication plus its antecedent yields the consequent.
